description: Origin header values sent to a CORS policy that allows credentials. Your function decides whether to echo the origin in Access-Control-Allow-Origin.
convention: Called as fn(origin). Rejected = throws or returns false/null/undefined. true = the request origin is echoed. A string = that string is sent as Access-Control-Allow-Origin.
oracle: An attack passes if it is rejected, or if the value sent is exactly one of allowed_origins (and not the attacker's origin). A legit input passes if the value sent equals the input.

attacks.why: arbitrary origin; reflecting it with credentials hands every visitor's session to the attacker
sandboxed iframes and data: URLs send Origin: null; allowlisting 'null' lets any site in
defeats startsWith and unanchored regex checks
defeats endsWith('trusted.example') without a dot boundary
unescaped '.' in a regex matches any character
scheme downgrade: an attacker on the network can inject script into the http origin
a different port is a different origin (often a dev server or admin tool)
unlisted subdomain; with a *.trusted.example wildcard, any XSS or takeover on any subdomain reads your API
trailing-dot hostname is a distinct origin
browsers always send a lowercased origin; accepting this means you normalize somewhere you shouldn't
